mainEntity.name: Is it better to convert an existing garage or build a new secondary dwelling unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Converting an existing garage into a secondary dwelling unit typically costs less and finishes faster than building a brand-new detached structure. A garage already provides an existing slab, framing, and roof, which saves substantial structural construction time. However, a garage conversion trades away vehicle parking and workshop space, while requiring major upgrades such as leveling uneven slabs, adding insulation, updating drywall, and running brand-new plumbing lines. A ground-up addition preserves garage storage and offers complete layout flexibility, though it involves full foundation excavation, exterior stucco or siding, and roofing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Converting a garage saves structural costs by using an existing frame and roof, but building new allows full layout flexibility without sacrificing covered vehicle parking.
